episode_title: How Advisory Accounting Could Turn Your Tax Clients into $2K Per Month Retainers with Dyanna Salcedo

real_qa.q: What is the average monthly retainer that CFO advisors at The CFO Project charge their clients?
real_qa.r: At the CFO Project, they recommend that CFO advisors charge a monthly retainer because they are driving value and driving the bank account balance for their clients. The average retainer that CFO advisors charge is about $2,000 a month. With just five clients, a sole practitioner can build a six-figure recurring revenue business.

real_qa.q: How many small businesses in the United States fail before reaching their fifth birthday according to The CFO Project?
real_qa.r: There are 36 million small businesses in the United States, and half of which will not make it to their fifth birthday. This is the statistic that The CFO Project aims to help small business owners defy by providing CFO advisory services.
real_qa.requete: small businesses fail fifth birthday statistics

real_qa.q: What are the 12 cash flow drivers that The CFO Project teaches accountants to track with clients each month?
real_qa.r: The CFO Project has defined 12 cashflow drivers that accountants and bookkeepers track every single month with clients, showing them where they are on track, off track, or at risk. The advisors then tie those drivers back to the business owner's specific goals—for example, needing to pay tuition for a child that year—and ask the client to focus on those key areas for the next 30 days.

real_qa.q: What two main fears do accounting firm owners express about AI and automation according to Dyanna Salcedo?
real_qa.r: The two primary fears Dyanna hears from accountants and bookkeepers are: first, the fear that AI and automation of compliance work will come for their jobs and roles, especially if they stay in the compliance lane; and second, the opposite narrative—a rejection of AI based on distrust, with people saying AI is inaccurate, cannot do math, and hallucinates. Salcedo emphasizes that embracing AI tools strategically can actually become a tailwind for stepping into advisory work.
real_qa.requete: AI fears accounting compliance jobs automation

real_qa.q: What is the competence-confidence loop that The CFO Project uses to help new CFO advisors overcome nervousness?
real_qa.r: The CFO Project teaches a competence-confidence loop: when a new CFO advisor takes their first step toward stepping into the advisory role—even when nervous or uncertain—they will learn something from that action which improves their confidence. That improved confidence then allows them to feel more comfortable taking a second step, creating an upward cycle of competence and confidence over time.

real_qa.q: What common obstacles prevent accountants and bookkeepers from successfully transitioning to advisory services?
real_qa.r: Dyanna identifies four main obstacles: creating capacity—often due to tax season demands or heavy bookkeeping client loads; lacking a repeatable process, which causes practitioners to hit a scaling ceiling; identity issues—people not yet seeing themselves as advisors, which The CFO Project addresses through dedicated mindset modules and peer groups led by executive coaches; and fear of selling, since advisory services require a different business development motion than tax or bookkeeping services.

guest.bio_context: Dyanna Salcedo served in the U.S. Army as a young adult, then built a career in finance on Wall Street as an analyst at BlackRock in the portfolio risk group covering fixed income, and later as an investment banker at Citi covering power and utilities. In 2016, she left her Wall Street position to join a regional dairy company based in New York City as head of finance and operations, where she managed P&L and team responsibilities. She subsequently founded her own fractional CFO advisory firm before joining The CFO Project last year to align with their mission to eradicate small business failure.
